Stated Claim / Post Context:
Elon Musk threatens Hillary Clinton's podcast partner Kara Swisher with prison after she claimed to know 'what's coming for him' if Democrats take power

With the midterm elections approaching in what is projected to be a 'blue wave,' the Trump ally appears to have little tolerance for criticism and fired online against tech journalist Kara Swisher.

Actual Article Body:
By VICTOR HELLER, US REPORTER and NATASHA ANDERSON, US SENIOR NEWS REPORTER

Published:  16:31 AEDT, 22 October 2026   |  Updated:  01:37 AEDT, 23 October 2026

Elon Musk has threatened Hillary Clinton's former podcast partner with prison after she claimed to know 'what's coming for him' if Democrats take power in the midterm elections.

Tech journalist Kara Swisher, who launched the High Stakes podcast with Clinton just last week, appeared on The Bulwark podcast and suggested Democrats should investigate Musk if they gain control of both chambers of Congress in November.

Swisher even went so far as to say that Musk would already have been sent to jail if Trump's Democratic challenger Kamala Harris had won the presidential election in 2024.

'Under Kamala Harris, he might be in jail right now, right?' Swisher said. 'And that's not because she's some avenging fury. It's because there is a lot of questions around different companies of his.'

The Tesla and SpaceX founder seemed to have little tolerance for Swisher's criticism and warned that she 'live by the sword, die by the sword.'

'Sounds like Swisher really wants to go to prison,' he wrote on his platform X.

In a separate post, he added: 'Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets.'

Musk's warning comes just days after his first wife, Justine Musk, appeared on Swisher's podcast and divulged details about the tech mogul's alleged 'suicidal' mindset, obsession with being an 'engineer' and his 'intense drive.'

Tesla and SpaceX founder Elon Musk was furious and threatened journalist and Hillary Clinton podcast pal Kara Swisher with prison after she criticized him online

Swisher said on a podcast when talking about Musk: 'Under Kamala Harris, he might be in jail right now, right?' She continued: 'And that's not because she's some avenging fury. It's because there is a lot of questions around different companies of his'

The world's first trillionaire took his upset about Swisher's remarks to social media. Source: @elonmusk/X

During her appearance on The Bulwark, Swisher claimed that Musk could be in trouble following the projected to be a 'blue wave' victory for Democrats next month,

She alleged that the agencies affected by the cuts Musk made when he was running the Department of Government Efficiency would start investigating his many companies.

Swisher continued: 'If Donald Trump loses the Senate, I would be worried if I were him even though how rich he is.

'He has a very big sense of fate. And I think it's coming for him. And real hard.'

Swisher's comments reached more than 2.4 million views on X, but Musk's response got about 574,000 views as of Wednesday night and sparked strong reactions.

One asked: 'Why would he be in jail for? He hasn't broken the law.'

Another calmed down the entrepreneur, saying: 'No worries, Kamala is NEVER going to be President.'

Polls are projecting that next month's Midterm elections could hand the Democrats both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Meanwhile, top Republicans insist those surveys are skewed and that the GOP will do far better than predicted.

The Daily Mail contacted Swisher for comment.

Swisher launched the High Stakes podcast with Hillary Clinton just last week

Musk's warning comes just days after his first wife, Justine Musk, (pictured) appeared on Swisher's podcast and divulged details about the tech mogul's alleged 'suicidal' mindset, obsession with being an 'engineer' and his 'intense drive'

Musk has poured more than $276 million into Republican groups as the party faces a challenging environment in advance of the midterm elections.

The development comes as it was reported Musk ordered a reduction in Starlink satellite services for Ukraine even as the tech billionaire claimed any limits on the communications system would ultimately have come from the president.

Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv's drones useless, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Kyiv has accused Washington of deliberately slowing speeds at which Starshield, a Starlink satellite network for national security services, can be used effectively, a charge denied last week by US President Donald Trump.

Musk had previously said that 'any limits on speed or usage' of Starshield systems were 'decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,' referring to Mr Trump.

Trump has denied ordering a reduction in speeds on Starshield after Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said that.

The president, who last week called on Zelensky to resign, also criticized Zelensky for not accepting the terms he said he had offered during their infamous televised argument in the Oval Office in February 2025.

Relations plunged back into a deep freeze earlier this month after Trump suddenly announced his deal with Russia for diesel, as part of his efforts to lower oil prices sent soaring by his Iran war.

The President wrote to Congress that the move was in the national interest, undoing legislation he signed just last month and named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

Destroyed cars in the courtyard of an apartment block following a Russian attack in Kyiv

President Donald Trump, right, shakes the hand of Russia's President Vladimir Putin during a joint press conference at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska in August 2025

Trump has also refused to blame Putin for starting the Ukraine war – putting him at loggerheads with the UK and other allies over the conflict.

Ukraine reacted with dismay after Trump also waived sanctions against Russia's war machine and appeared to once again pivot to Putin.

The feud spiraled as Zelensky accused Trump of weakness, and then alleged that the United States was deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying the delivery of vital interceptor missiles.

The Ukraine war was triggered after Putin ordered the invasion of Russia's neighbor in 2022. Putin ordered up to 200,000 troops into Ukraine in an attempt to overthrow its pro-Western government.

Since then, Ukraine has suffered hundreds of thousands of deaths while missiles and drones regularly rain down on the capital Kyiv.

Starlink satellites, operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, provide high-speed internet to Ukraine's military. It is vital for communications on the battlefield and effective drone warfare.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Washington had no prior knowledge of the Starlink slowdown.

'The President has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk,' Mr Rubio said during his trip to India.

'That's a private company; the President doesn't run that company and can't direct that company to do anything... I'm telling you, there was no foreknowledge.'

On Tuesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the Pentagon had not directed any changes to Starshield, saying: 'We haven't pulled anything back.'

Elon Musk approached Donald Trump with the idea of slowing down Starlink in Ukraine, inhibiting its ability to intercept Russian drone and missile attacks, sources have claimed

Russia strikes on the Ukraine capital of Kyiv back in August

Musk on Tuesday also suggested that a merger of Tesla and SpaceX could soon be in the works after SpaceX reported a bigger quarterly profit than expected.

The company posted a profit for the three months through September of $4.4 billion, or 35 cents per share, reversing a year-ago loss and easily topping Wall Street's expectations. Revenue soared to $14.6 billion, up 161 percent.

On a conference call with analysts, Musk said special committees of independent directors at both SpaceX and Tesla have been set up to study the idea at the request of shareholders.

He added that he could not take part in their talks because he has a conflict of interest.

Musk is chief executive of both companies, and also serves as chairman and chief technology officer of SpaceX.

The trillionaire told analysts that for next month's launch of its Starship rocket, SpaceX will attempt to grab both the booster and ship with mechanical arms upon return to base, a key step toward demonstrating it can reuse the massive spacecraft.

'The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle,' Musk said, calling the attempt, if successful, 'a massive technology milestone.'

SpaceX hopes to get Starship on a regular launch pattern in preparation for NASA's upcoming lunar missions.

Earlier this week, Musk pledged to give one share of SpaceX to 'every kid in America' next year

The news of the potential merger came after Musk pledged to give one share of SpaceX to 'every kid in America' next year.

The offer came Monday, one day after artificial intelligence company Anthropic announced in a social media post that it will commit 5 percent of its shares to a new 'public benefit' fund.

In a response to that Sunday post, Musk wrote: 'I recommend giving the shares directly to the public.'

With approximately 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, that would put the value of Musk's pledge at about $10.66 billion.

Musk did not provide further details on how his share pledge will be carried out but did add in his post that 'This will be the first of many.'

Hillary Clinton Blames Angry Voters for Defeat; Calls for 'Sacred Resistance' Against Trump

Hillary Clinton, in an event discussing her faith at a Manhattan Church Thursday night, partly blamed angry voters for her defeat and called for “sacred resistance” against President Trump.
The post Hillary Clinton Blames Angry Voters for Defeat; Calls for ‘Sacred Resistance’ Against Trump appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
NEW YORK CITY — Hillary Clinton, in an event discussing her faith at a Manhattan Church Thursday night, partly blamed angry voters for her defeat and called for “sacred resistance” against President Trump.

The event, “An Evening with Hillary Clinton to Benefit Camp Olmsted,” was a fundraiser for the children’s camp, during which Clinton was going to discuss her faith with her pastor, Bill Shillady, who in turn was supposed to discuss his new book, Strong for a Moment Like This: The Daily Devotions of Hillary Rodham Clinton.

However, days before the event, the publisher yanked the book and destroyed remaining copies after it found multiple examples of plagiarism.

Each ticket was to include a copy of the book, but ticket holders received refunds for that part of the ticket for the event at Riverside Church. Shillady was not in attendance and was replaced by Rev. Ginger Gaines-Cirelli.

But while Clinton was not promoting Shillady’s book and spent much of the roughly 35-minute discussion talking about her faith and how it affected her post-election demeanor, she did promote her own upcoming campaign post-mortem book, What Happened, and mentioned it multiple times.

The packed crowd was treated to Clinton’s blaming angry voters for why she lost in November.

“I knew there were people who were angry and people who had resentments. I understood that and could see that. But I couldn’t believe – and I’m just not wired to think – that the best way for a leader to bring people together and solve problems is to stoke that anger and to feed that resentment,” she said to wild applause.

She went on to say that while that anger is often justified, the leadership she was offering was not enough for the angry people – perhaps referring to those voters she once called a “basket of deplorables”:

I think the kind of leadership I was offering was not satisfying enough for certain people, and it wasn’t enough for me to say, ‘Look, I understand, and here’s what I want to do to help’ if I didn’t display more anger so that they could feel I got their anger. And I feel that is a legitimate question about what happened in that campaign in 2016 and something I struggled with because I don’t think anger is a strategy. It is certainly justified in the face of what we see oftentimes in our society, but I think leaders, whether it’s in church or in politics, should be looking for ways to find common ground, or even higher ground, and not to create scapegoats and stoke hatred, bigotry, and prejudice, and the like.

Asked what she would recommend to “people of faith” who want to resist Trump, she pointed to the Gaines-Cirelli strategy of engaging in “sacred resistance” — a form of church-based organizing to push back against Trump’s policies.

“For people of faith, that is one way to conceptualize how you can be active on behalf of causes, on behalf of people who need your voice and your support,” Clinton said.

She said her new PAC, Onward Together, is a part of that:

Through Onward Together … [we want to help] find the next generation of concerned citizens, activists, organizers, to give them funding, to give them guidance, because we need a lot of activity at the grassroots level. We need people in every community standing up and speaking out. There is so much to be concerned about. Yes, I am okay, but I am worried. I am worried that we face a continuing deliberate effort to undermine our values and our institutions as Americans, and it is something we cannot stay silent about or be on the sidelines about.

Clinton went on to call on people to “resist, insist, persist, and enlist.”

Clinton’s book What Happened is out September 12, and teasers have hinted at an angry book that blames a wide range of people for her defeat in November.
